title: [CQ-RF01] Persistent daemon provenance across IDE restarts
description:
Objective: after an IDE restart, a protected-profile project can reconnect to a daemon that the IDE itself spawned earlier, instead of refusing it. Today it is refused by design, because spawn provenance (pid plus start instant, or the direct parent) lives only in memory. This is CQ-R01's follow-up 1, from the architect note on CQ-R13. Its design is in Serena memory decision-protected-runtime-selection.

Created by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30, when the human moved the non-gating R01 follow-ups out of CQ-R13 into this epic.

Deliverable:
- In the JetBrains plugin, change MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt and RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt as CQ-R01 landed them, under moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/.
- Persist each protected spawn record outside the repository, in the IDE system directory, with owner-only access: {project path, pid, process start instant, installed daemon path}.
- In doConnect, accept an already-running daemon only when its live pid and start instant match a stored record for this project and the installed daemon.
- A missing, mismatched, foreign-project or unreadable record refuses exactly as today.
- Prune records whose process is gone.
- Tests go in the existing Kotlin test classes: MoeDaemonSupervisorTest and RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.

Out of scope:
- the downgrade pin (CQ-RF02);
- replacing an unverified daemon (CQ-RF03);
- the Windows restart race (CQ-RF04);
- VS Code (CQ-RF06);
- .moe edits;
- enabling verified-local.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun" (= cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test; this WSL host has no Linux JDK)
definitionOfDone: After an IDE restart, a daemon the IDE spawned under the protected profile is accepted only when its live pid and start instant match a stored provenance record for this project and the installed daemon. Shown by tests.
A missing, mismatched, foreign-project or unreadable record refuses the connection exactly as today. The store is outside the repository with owner-only access. Shown by tests.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
New generic owner-only store, tests first: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/ProtectedStateStore.kt. It is shared on purpose. RF02's persistent downgrade pin will reuse it; that sibling was asked in #architects to depend on this task.

API:
- `class ProtectedStateStore internal constructor(val root: Path)`.
- `companion fun forIde(): ProtectedStateStore?`: `Paths.get(PathManager.getSystemPath(), "moe", "protected-state")` when `ApplicationManager.getApplication() != null`, else null. Plain JUnit runs have no Application, so they never touch a real IDE directory. Any exception also gives null.
- `fun usableFor(basePath: String): Boolean`, which is `RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject(root.toString(), basePath)`. A runIde/test sandbox system dir under this repository is inside the project when the repo is the project, so it is refused.
- `fun read(name: String): String?`:
  - null when the file is absent;
  - throws an Untrusted exception when the root dir or the file is not owner-only, is not a regular file (checked with NOFOLLOW_LINKS, so links are refused) or is over 64 KiB (read at most cap+1 bytes);
  - otherwise returns the UTF-8 text.
- `fun write(name: String, text: String)`:
  - create root (and parents) owner-only;
  - create a temp file in root, owner-only BEFORE any byte is written;
  - write, then `Files.move(tmp, target, ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)`;
  - delete the temp file on any failure, and rethrow.
- `fun delete(name: String)`.
- `name` must match `[0-9a-f]{64}\.json`; anything else throws. Callers pass a sha-256 file name, so no path from input is ever joined.

Owner-only:
- POSIX: dir exactly rwx------ and file exactly rw-------. Create with `PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute`, then call `Files.setPosixFilePermissions` explicitly.
- Windows (no POSIX view): `AclFileAttributeView` with one ALLOW entry for the file's owner (`view.owner`) carrying every AclEntryPermission, set via `view.acl = listOf(...)`.
- The read-side check is the same definition: POSIX permissions exactly as above; ACL non-empty with every entry ALLOW for the owner principal.
- Neither view supported: write throws and read is untrusted.

Error handling: this class may throw, but only typed exceptions with a short message naming the broken rule and never file contents. Its single caller (step 2) catches every one.

Tests in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt (TemporaryFolder; Windows-only and POSIX-only cases guarded with assumeTrue on the supported view, so each OS runs its branch):
(a) After a write, root and file are owner-only by the definition above, and read returns the text.
(b) A file loosened afterwards reads as Untrusted: POSIX chmod 644; Windows an extra ALLOW entry for another principal, e.g. the Everyone group via `lookupPrincipalByGroupName("Everyone")`, with assumeTrue when lookup fails.
(c) Other failures:
- an absent file is null;
- an oversize file (cap+1 bytes) is Untrusted;
- a symlinked file is Untrusted, with assumeTrue on link support (reuse the `symlink` helper);
- a bad name throws.
(d) usableFor is false for a root inside the project and true for one outside.
(e) forIde() is null in this plain JUnit JVM.
implementationPlan.note: NEW com.moe.util.ProtectedStateStore (155 lines, LF): internal ctor(root), companion forIde() (null without Application, or on any exception), usableFor = isOutsideProject, read/write/delete with names limited to [0-9a-f]{64}\.json (IllegalArgumentException otherwise), typed Untrusted : IOException. Owner-only = POSIX exactly rwx------/rw------- or ACL non-empty with every entry ALLOW for the owner; write sets it explicitly (dir + temp file before any byte), re-checks it and refuses to persist if it did not hold, then ATOMIC_MOVE+REPLACE_EXISTING, temp deleted on any failure. Read: NOFOLLOW_LINKS attribute check + NOFOLLOW_LINKS open, root must be a real directory (a link or Windows junction root is refused), 64 KiB cap (cap+1 read). Additions beyond the plan, all fail-closed: write refuses text over the cap; a write re-restricts an existing root (heals a loosened root; a loosened file stays untrusted until replaced). Tests PS1-PS5 in RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest (plan (a)-(e); named PS* because P1-P4 already name the profile tests): PS1 write/read/replace/delete + owner-only (independent check, exactly one ALLOW owner ACE on Windows); PS2 loosened file AND loosened root -> Untrusted, healed by next write; PS3 absent/no-root null, exactly-cap ok, cap+1 Untrusted, write over cap refused keeping old bytes, 9 bad names throw on read/write/delete and write nothing, linked file + linked root refused (root write too). PS4 usableFor; PS5 forIde null. RED (stub): 5 failed/34. GREEN: `cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.util.RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest --rerun"` exit 0, XML 34 tests 0 skipped 0 failures (Windows; no POSIX branch exercised here, CI Linux runs it). Windows ACL confirmed: setAcl leaves exactly the single owner entry.

implementationPlan.description:
Persist and verify spawn records in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt. Tests go in RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest beside V1-V3.

- `SpawnRecord` gains `val daemon: String? = null`, the comparable real path of the installed daemon/index.js. Existing constructor calls keep compiling.
- `recordProtectedSpawn(basePath, handle, installedDaemon: File? = null)`. `remember(...)` keeps its pruning and, when the record has a daemon and the store is usable for basePath, also persists.
- Store access: `@Volatile internal var store: () -> ProtectedStateStore? = { ideStore }`, with `ideStore` a lazy `ProtectedStateStore.forIde()`. `resetForTest()` restores the default. Add `internal fun forgetSessionForTest()`, which clears only `pinned` and `spawns` and simulates an IDE restart.
- File: `sha256Hex(projectKey(basePath)) + ".json"` holding `{"version":1,"project":<projectKey>,"records":[{"pid":<long>,"start":<Instant.toString()>,"supervisor":<bool>,"daemon":<string>}]}`.
- Read STRICT: generalize parseStrict with a label so messages stop saying project.json. Validate every type: version exactly 1, project equal to this key (a foreign-project file is refused), pid > 0, `Instant.parse` start, boolean supervisor, string daemon. Any violation makes the whole file untrusted.
- `verifyProvenance(basePath, pid, facts = ::liveFacts, installedDaemon: File? = null)`. The new parameter is LAST so the positional calls keep compiling.
  - The in-memory check is unchanged.
  - If it does not verify and installedDaemon is non-null and resolves (comparable real path), load the persisted records for this key. Prune each record whose `facts(pid)?.start != start`, then rewrite the file, or delete it when empty.
  - Accept only a record with an equal daemon path whose (pid, start) equals the live daemon's, or whose supervisor (pid, start) equals the live direct parent's. These are the same rules as in memory, so a daemon still cannot vouch for itself or its children.
  - On accept, add the record to memory, and add and persist the child record as today's in-memory parent path does, so the daemon stays verifiable after its supervisor dies.
- Error handling: every store failure falls back to today's refusal text exactly and never throws: absent, untrusted, IO error, store not usable, installedDaemon null or unresolvable. A write failure keeps the in-memory record only. Log the failure (warn for untrusted or write failures, debug for absent).
- Serialize store read-modify-write with one lock (`@Synchronized` helper or a private lock object). Different JVMs only meet through the atomic move.

Tests use fake facts with T0/T1, a store in a TemporaryFolder outside the project, and `forgetSessionForTest()` between "sessions":
(P1) A supervisor record with daemon D, persisted, then forget. Its child verifies with installedDaemon=D, and the child is now persisted. Forget again and drop the supervisor from facts: the child still verifies.
(P2) Each of these refuses with exactly `refusal(pid)`, the refusal text that existing tests already use for this case:
- installed daemon D2;
- installedDaemon null;
- another project;
- a file under this project's name whose project field names another;
- a reused pid (start T1, stored T0);
- malformed JSON, a BOM, trailing content, version 2, a missing or extra-typed field, oversize;
- a loosened file;
- a store rooted inside the project (nothing is ever written there).
(P3) Pruning: a record whose pid is gone, and one whose start changed, are removed from the file after the next verify. The file is deleted when no record is left.
(P4) V1-V3, S1 and S5 stay green unchanged. They use no store: resetForTest restores the default, which is null in JUnit.
implementationPlan.note: Persisted provenance in RuntimeSelectionPolicy. SpawnRecord gains daemon (installed daemon's comparable real path via installedDaemonKey); recordProtectedSpawn(basePath, handle, installedDaemon) and remember persist records that name their daemon (never throws; store failure keeps the record in memory, warn log). verifyProvenance(basePath, pid, facts, installedDaemon): session rules first (unchanged; the in-session parent path now also persists the child, since Process.destroy on Windows orphans the _run child); else, when installedDaemon resolves and the store is outside the project, load <sha256(projectKey)>.json under storeLock, prune records whose pid+start no longer match (rewrite, or delete when empty), and accept only own (pid,start) or a child of a persisted supervisor whose record names the installed daemon; accepted records + child go to memory, child persisted. Strict file codec: STRICT reader, no BOM/trailing content, exact fields {version,project,records} and {pid,start,supervisor,daemon}, canonical version 1, project == this key, positive canonical pid, ISO start, boolean supervisor, string daemon; any violation refuses the whole file with the exact existing refusal. persist replaces an untrusted file (its records never trusted); a failed load never rewrites during verify. parseStrict takes a label (default project.json, existing messages unchanged). Tests: PP1, PP2a+PP2b (plan P2, split to keep functions under 50 lines; PP2b also proves the valid file verifies before each mutation and the exact-cap file verifies before the one-byte overflow; PP2a also refuses a valid file placed in an in-project store), PP3 (= plan P1-P3; 'PP' avoids clashing with existing profile tests P1-P4). V3's call now names facts = {...}: the new trailing installedDaemon parameter would otherwise capture the trailing lambda; semantics unchanged. RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt is 467 lines (>300 guideline): the plan limits the change to five files and the codec needs the private parseStrict/UntrustedSetting; no function exceeds 25 lines. implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
(a) Error handling: every failure path fails closed to today's exact refusal text: absent, untrusted, IO error, store unusable, a null or unresolvable installed daemon. Nothing throws out of RuntimeSelectionPolicy or the supervisor.
(b) Only IDE-written, owner-only files are trusted. A planted or loosened file, a symlink, an in-project root or a foreign-project file is refused. The name is a sha-256 hex and never a path from input.
(c) Start-instant equality defeats pid reuse for stored records exactly as for in-memory ones. Only a supervisor record vouches for a child.
(d) Concurrency: read-modify-write sits under one lock and the atomic replace means a reader never sees a partial file. Two projects use two files.
(e) LEGACY selection, activation and restart are byte-for-byte unchanged. V1-V3, S1-S5, R2 and G3 stay green.
(f) No data from the repository's .moe/daemon.json other than the pid reaches the store. The store never names the project's files.
(g) The diff touches only the five planned files. No .moe edits, no forbidden patterns, LF line endings. KDoc on the new class explains why the store exists and that RF02 reuses it.
Fix anything found, re-run the step 4 gate under the lease if any byte changed, then complete_task with the step 4 evidence.
implementationPlan.note: I ran the adversarial self-review on the task-scoped diff. No bytes changed in this step: every edit predates the step-4 gate at 07:35:52Z, and the main files match their pre-mutation sha256. The step-4 gate therefore stands as the evidence. (a) Every failure path fails closed to the existing refusal text, asserted with exact strings in PP2a, PP2b and S6: absent file, untrusted file, IO error, unusable or in-project store, and a null or unresolvable installed daemon. verifyProvenance, recordProtectedSpawn and persist catch everything, and activationRefusal only composes installedArtifact (never throws) with verifyProvenance. Gson is 2.14.0, so a deeply nested file hits the reader's nesting limit and becomes a caught IOException. (b) Only an owner-only regular file reached without a link, at most 64 KiB, named by a sha-256 hex and passing the strict schema is trusted. Planted, loosened, linked or junctioned, in-project and foreign-project files are all refused (PS2-PS4, PP2a, PP2b). (c) Stored records need pid+start equality in both the prune and the match (M2 killed), and only a supervisor record vouches for a child (M10 killed after the new PP2a case). (d) Each read-modify-write runs under storeLock. The temp file plus ATOMIC_MOVE means a reader never sees a partial file. Each project has its own hashed file. (e) LEGACY returns before any policy or store call; the spawn records only when isProtected; the restart LEGACY branch is untouched. V1-V3, S1-S5, R2 and G3 are green in the full gate. (f) Only daemon.json's pid enters verification. Persisted values come from OS facts, the IDE's own basePath key and the installed daemon's real path. The file name is a hash, never a project file or a path from input. (g) Only the five planned files are touched. There are no .moe edits by me, no forbidden patterns, LF only, and the KDoc on ProtectedStateStore explains why the store exists and that CQ-RF02 reuses it. Theoretical risks I considered and did not fix: (1) Two IDE JVMs writing the same project file concurrently can lose a record; that fails closed to today's refusal. (2) The JDK exposes no ACL view on macOS, so extended macOS ACLs are not inspected; the POSIX 700/600 modes are set explicitly and checked. (3) An IDE running as root could trust an attacker-owned 600 file, but only if an ancestor of the IDE system directory were writable by that attacker. For a non-root user, readable plus owner-only already implies the user is the owner. (4) A JVM crash mid-write can leave a state-*.tmp file; it never matches the name pattern and is never read. Size: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt is 467 lines, kept in one file by the plan's five-file limit, with no function over 25 lines. The test file was already far over 300 lines.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Chosen: a generic owner-only ProtectedStateStore in the IDE system dir, with spawn-record persistence on top inside RuntimeSelectionPolicy. RF02's pin reuses the store, so there is no second storage mechanism.
2) Rejected: IntelliJ PersistentStateComponent / PropertiesComponent. Those write into IDE config XML with default permissions; owner-only access cannot be enforced or checked.
3) Rejected: storing provenance under the project's .moe. The rails forbid it, and it is repository content anyone can edit.
4) Rejected: trusting daemon-reported provenance or argv. The design memory (decision-protected-runtime-selection) forbids caller-minted evidence, and Node can rewrite argv.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Provenance today is in-memory per project key: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.spawns with SpawnRecord(pid, start, supervisor). verifyProvenance accepts the daemon's own (pid, start) or its direct parent's supervisor record, and records the child. MoeDaemonSupervisor.activationRefusal is called by MoeProjectService.doConnect and by stopDaemonForRestart. protectedDaemonCommand yields [node, daemon/index.js (real path), start, --project, basePath]. Test helpers in RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest: protectedFixture, supervisorFor, IdleProcess, fakeHandle, refusal(pid), installedLayout, symlink, T0/T1; resetForTest is called @Before/@After. The Gradle test task strips the IntelliJ platform argument provider, so there is no Application in these JUnit tests.
planningNotes.risks:
The Windows ACL behaviour must be confirmed on the real Windows FS: setAcl replaces the DACL, and the test asserts the result. If inherited ACEs reappear, refuse to persist and report it rather than weakening the owner-only check.

The POSIX permission branch only runs in CI's Linux job, since the local gate is Windows. Label which cases skipped.

Sibling overlap: RF02 (being planned by architect-4ae016fb, asked to depend on this task) and probably RF03/RF04 touch the same files; serialize them via dependsOn.
